Job Description

The Role

We are seeking a seasoned and technically strong Director of Software Engineering to lead the development and evolution of Operations Workstation platform. This is an exciting opportunity to be at the forefront of a transformational modernization journey — reimagining and rebuilding a mission-critical operations workstation into a best-in-class, next-generation platform for our brokerage operations users.

You will play a defining role in shaping the future of how operations users interact with technology — replacing aging systems with a modern, high-performance, container-based operations workstation that leverages platform interoperability capabilities to integrate seamlessly across enterprise systems, tools, and financial data services. Beyond engineering delivery, you will own the delivery roadmap, drive technology strategy and lead a high-performing team through a complex, multi-phase modernization.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, Roadmap and Planning

Assist VP of Engineering in developing and implementing a multi-year technology strategy for Brokerage Operations workstation
Closely partner with Product Manager and VP of Engineering to build a delivery roadmap balancing modernization, operationally driven initiatives, regulatory compliance, and operational stability.
Translate strategic intent into actionable engineering plans with clear milestones, resource requirements, and success metrics
Lead structured planning and prioritization processes — balancing new capability delivery, platform modernization, and operational stability.
Partner with product management, UX, operations, and business stakeholders to align technology delivery with business goals
Drive consistency across platform experience, ensuring that interop-connected applications and workstation components deliver a seamless, integrated user experience for operations users
Establish design principles and platform standards that guide engineering decisions and ensure the workstation evolves as a coherent, best-in-class product
Communicate technical strategy and delivery roadmaps clearly to both technical and non-technical executive audiences

Organizational Leadership

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of engineers
Drive talent development, resource planning, and associate growth.
Foster a culture of engineering excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement
Inspire and align the engineering team around a shared modernization vision, maintaining momentum and morale through a complex, multi-phase transformation

Delivery and Execution

Own end-to-end engineering delivery — from backlog refinement and sprint planning through release management and production deployment
Drive a high-performance delivery culture that balances velocity with quality, reliability, and security in a regulated financial environment
Establish and monitor KPIs for delivery health, system performance, reliability, and modernization progress — using data to drive continuous improvement
Remove organizational blockers and dependencies that impede engineering execution, escalating appropriately and decisively
Drive incident management, root cause analysis, and operational stability improvements across the platform
Own technology lifecycle management and technology product management — ensuring all applications and platform components are maintained to the latest standards, current versions, and best practices.
Champion the integration of artificial intelligence and AI-assisted development tooling — including AI code generation, automated testing, intelligent code review, and predictive analytics — to meaningfully accelerate the software delivery cycle and increase engineering throughput
Identify and embed AI-driven automation across the SDLC, from requirements analysis and design through development, QA, deployment, and monitoring — reducing manual toil and compressing time-to-production

Required

The Expertise and Skills You Bring

10–12 years in software engineering leadership, including experience at the Director level.
Experience in complex, multi-year transformation programs.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Demonstrated domain knowledge in brokerage, financial services operations, back-office processing
Experience building and leading high-performing engineering teams in a fast-paced, regulated environment
Strong proficiency in Angular and modern front-end development practices
Solid understanding of Java and Spring Boot for back-end services and API development
Experience with platform interoperability (interop) design and implementation — enabling cross-application context sharing, event broadcasting, and workflow integration in a financial desktop or workstation environment
Hands-on experience with container-based application architecture — understanding how UI workstation components are packaged, deployed, and managed within a containerized model
Proven ability to work with and modernize legacy technology stacks while maintaining system stability and operational continuity
Strong understanding of UI/UX principles as applied to complex operations workstations
Experience with CI/CD pipelines and DevOps practices in a regulated financial environment
Solid grasp of software architecture, distributed systems, and real-time data platforms

Preferred

Experience with brokerage back-office systems
Knowledge of regulatory frameworks such as FINRA, SEC Rule 15c3, or SOX compliance requirements

Trek Travel provides global cycling, hiking, and walking vacations of a lifetime with the goal of helping more people actively explore and experience the world. We are looking for a Director of Technology to lead our technology team and shape how technology powers the way we design, sell, and deliver world-class bike and hiking trips. The ideal candidate is both a strong people leader and a practical technologist - someone who can inspire a team, build trusted relationships across departments, and implement modern systems and AI tools that fit seamlessly into our business. This is a full-time, exempt position based at our Madison, Wisconsin office, with a hybrid schedule and regular in-office presence expected. This position reports directly to the President of Trek Travel.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT NOT LIMITED TO:

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, and develop the technology team, including hiring, goal setting, performance management, and career development across IT, ecommerce, and development staff.
Provide support, training, and guidance to internal and external technology users, assessing computing needs and system requirements.

Strategy & Roadmap

Translate company vision into an enterprise systems strategy and multi-year technology roadmap, partnering with department heads and senior leadership to align technology with operational and strategic goals.
Lead planning and execution of company-wide technology initiatives, including project management, change management, and staff training across departments.

Systems, Infrastructure & AI

Own the architecture and integrations connecting our booking, ecommerce, ERP, CRM, and financial systems, including performance, reliability, and upgrades of core business systems and the Microsoft Power Platform environment.
Lead the ecommerce and software development functions, setting technical direction and quality standards for the team.
Develop and execute Trek Travel's AI strategy and governance standards, identifying high-impact opportunities to improve workflows and productivity while safeguarding data privacy and security.
Own the company's reporting data model, serving as steward of a single source of truth for business metrics.

Security & Compliance

Own the information security program, including risk management, endpoint protection, access controls, MFA, patching, and least-privilege reviews
Ensure cybersecurity and regulatory compliance across guest booking and payment systems (PCI-DSS, GDPR, state privacy laws), including annual assessments, penetration testing, and remediation.
Deliver ongoing security awareness training and maintain a tested incident response and disaster recovery plan.

Budget & Vendor Management

Oversee the technology department budget and manage vendor, consultant, and SaaS relationships across the full lifecycle — from selection and negotiation to renewal and performance review.

WHAT ELSE WE'D LIKE TO SEE FROM YOU:

Bachelor's degree and 8+ years of progressive technology experience, including 3+ years leading and developing technical teams.
Deep technical experience across IT management, programming, ERP systems, database administration and security, and web/application development.
A practical, hands-on technologist with strong technical architecture instincts and a well-rounded background across development, data, security, infrastructure, ecommerce, CRM, and ERP.
Excellent communication and analytical skills, with a solution-oriented, “how can I help” attitude and strong troubleshooting instincts.
Values hospitality and customer service, with an interest in the active travel industry a plus.

TREK TRAVEL OFFERS:

A fast-paced, casual, motivating, and fun company culture where initiative and pro-activity are highly valued.
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
Short- and long-term disability and life insurance
Paid parental leave
401(k) with company match
Generous PTO, paid holidays, and volunteer time off
Rewards for sustainable commuting
Employee and outdoor industry discounts

At Trek Travel, we think outside the box, continuously improve, encourage feedback, and give it all we got, all the time, no exceptions. If you have what it takes to join our team and the desire to help shape Trek Travel's future, we wish you the best of luck and look forward to your application!

Job Description

Position Summary

Cloud/Systems is a key domain within Southland's Infrastructure organization, focused on enabling secure, scalable, and reliable cloud-first technology services across the enterprise. This role supports the company's growth by driving consistency in how cloud platforms, identity services, M365 foundational services, and core enterprise systems are designed, governed, and operated.

As the Director, Systems Engineering, you will lead the strategy, standardization, and ongoing improvement of Southland's cloud infrastructure and systems platforms. This includes Microsoft Azure, M365 foundational services, Entra ID, core identity capabilities, infrastructure automation, platform governance, and the operational practices required to keep enterprise systems reliable and secure.

The focus is simple: make it easier for teams to scale securely, integrate new business needs quickly, operate cloud services consistently, and reduce risk through strong architecture, automation, governance, and operational discipline.

You will work closely with Cybersecurity, Network, Platform Engineering, Support Services, business leaders, and key vendors to ensure cloud and systems platforms support how the company operates today and how it needs to grow. Travel to offices or project locations will be required depending on business needs.

Position Details

Cloud Architecture & Platform Strategy

Lead the development and governance of enterprise cloud architecture with primary focus on Microsoft Azure, M365 foundational services, and cloud-first infrastructure capabilities.
Define and enforce standards for cloud compute, storage, platform services, tenant configuration, cloud-side networking dependencies, and core enterprise systems.
Establish repeatable architecture patterns, landing zones, naming standards, tagging standards, service models, and reference architectures that support growth and consistency.
Drive modernization through infrastructure-as-code, automation, standardized service deployment, and simplification of legacy or inconsistent system practices.
Ensure cloud architecture balances scalability, security, cost efficiency, resilience, and operational supportability.
Provide technical direction for cloud platform decisions, ensuring designs align with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity standards, and business priorities.
Translate business growth plans into practical cloud and systems roadmap decisions that can scale across divisions, offices, and project environments.

Identity & Access Management

Own the enterprise identity strategy as a core control plane for access, security, and platform integration.
Lead governance of Entra ID, authentication methods, role-based access control, conditional access, identity lifecycle management, and enterprise access patterns.
Partner with Cybersecurity to align privileged access, zero trust enforcement, identity protection, and access monitoring with enterprise security requirements.
Ensure identity services are designed to scale with organizational growth, acquisitions, new offices, new applications, and changing compliance requirements.
Establish standards for administrative access, service accounts, groups, application integrations, and identity-related operational processes.
Drive consistent identity practices across M365, Azure, SaaS integrations, infrastructure platforms, and business-facing services.

Cloud Operations & Reliability

Own the operational performance, reliability, and availability of cloud and systems platforms under the Cloud/Systems function.
Establish monitoring, alerting, logging, and observability practices that allow teams to detect issues early and reduce business impact.
Lead operational maturity efforts including incident response coordination, problem management, root cause analysis, change management, and continuous improvement.
Define and enforce configuration management, lifecycle management, backup, recovery, patching, and service health practices for cloud and systems platforms.
Ensure operational practices are scalable and repeatable rather than dependent on tribal knowledge or one-off manual processes.
Partner with Support and Platform Engineering to ensure clean handoffs, escalation paths, and visibility into platform issues that impact users.

Automation & Infrastructure Engineering

Drive automation of infrastructure provisioning, platform configuration, reporting, and recurring operational tasks.
Establish infrastructure-as-code standards using appropriate tools such as Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or similar automation frameworks.
Promote reusable templates, modules, scripts, and deployment patterns that improve consistency and reduce manual effort.
Align infrastructure automation with change management, auditability, access control, and operational governance requirements.
Support the development of automated workflows for provisioning, deprovisioning, system configuration, and compliance reporting.
Create an engineering culture that favors repeatable, documented, and measurable solutions over ad hoc administration.

M365 Platform Governance & Administration

Own administration and platform governance of M365 foundational services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Exchange Online, OneDrive, and related tenant-level capabilities.
Ensure M365 services are configured consistently with enterprise standards for security, retention, provisioning, lifecycle management, and service integration.
Partner with Technology Delivery to support collaboration capabilities while maintaining Cloud/Systems ownership of tenant configuration, platform controls, and technical governance.
Define guardrails for site provisioning, storage, sharing, lifecycle, service settings, and administrative ownership across M365 services.
Support data governance requirements by implementing platform-level controls for retention, classification dependencies, auditability, and access management.
Ensure M365 configuration decisions are documented, supportable, and aligned with Cybersecurity, Legal, Compliance, and business needs.

Security & Compliance Integration

Partner with Cybersecurity to ensure cloud and systems platforms meet enterprise security, data protection, and compliance expectations.
Support implementation of controls for logging, monitoring, audit readiness, vulnerability management, secure configuration, and incident response.
Ensure cloud and systems platforms align with zero trust principles and applicable frameworks such as NIST, CMMC, or other regulatory requirements.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries between Cloud/Systems platform controls, Cybersecurity policy and monitoring, and Technology Delivery business enablement. Drive remediation of platform risks related to identity, configuration drift, excessive permissions, unsupported services, and inconsistent administration practices.

Vendor, Licensing & Cloud Financial Management

Manage relationships with cloud providers, Microsoft, service partners, and key enterprise platform vendors.
Oversee cloud consumption, licensing, cost visibility, and cost optimization practices in partnership with Finance, Procurement, and technology leadership.
Establish FinOps-aligned practices for cost accountability, forecasting, service usage review, and optimization of cloud and M365 investments.
Evaluate vendor capabilities, platform roadmaps, and service changes to determine practical value and risk for Southland.
Ensure contracts, licensing models, and platform decisions support scalability, reliability, compliance, and responsible cost management.

Leadership, Team Development & Governance

Build and lead a high-performing Cloud/Systems organization, including cloud engineering, systems engineering, identity, and M365 platform administration capabilities.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, service ownership, performance expectations, and development paths for team members.
Set priorities, manage staffing and budget needs, and align team capacity with enterprise initiatives and operational commitments.
Promote a culture of accountability, standardization, automation, documentation, and continuous improvement.
Serve as a strategic advisor to Infrastructure leadership by clearly communicating risks, tradeoffs, roadmap needs, resource constraints, and business impacts.
Develop governance practices that allow the organization to move quickly while maintaining secure, reliable, and supportable platforms.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in information technology, computer science, engineering, cybersecurity, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, enterprise infrastructure, or related technology leadership roles.
5+ years of experience leading technical teams, including responsibility for planning, staffing, performance management, budgeting, and prioritization of work.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure, M365, Entra ID, and cloud-first enterprise platform operations.
Deep understanding of identity and access management, including authentication, RBAC, conditional access, privileged access, group strategy, and identity lifecycle processes.
Experience designing and operating scalable cloud environments that support distributed companies, rapid growth, multiple offices, and diverse business needs.
Strong understanding of cloud operations, monitoring, incident response, change management, lifecycle management, backup/recovery, and service reliability practices.
Experience with infrastructure automation and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or similar platforms.

Description

The Senior Director of Enterprise Data Partners (EDP) – Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for the development, governance, and delivery of enterprise data and analytics products supporting revenue cycle, finance strategy, and accounting across the Mount Sinai Health System.

Own and scale a portfolio of enterprise data products and sources of truth, including datasets, semantic layers, dashboards, and benchmarking-integrated assets, with accountability for product vision, adoption, standardization, governance, and measurable impact on financial and operational outcomes and business value.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Job Description

Position Summary

Cloud/Systems is a key domain within Southland's Infrastructure organization, focused on enabling secure, scalable, and reliable cloud-first technology services across the enterprise. This role supports the company's growth by driving consistency in how cloud platforms, identity services, M365 foundational services, and core enterprise systems are designed, governed, and operated.

As the Director, Systems Engineering, you will lead the strategy, standardization, and ongoing improvement of Southland's cloud infrastructure and systems platforms. This includes Microsoft Azure, M365 foundational services, Entra ID, core identity capabilities, infrastructure automation, platform governance, and the operational practices required to keep enterprise systems reliable and secure.

The focus is simple: make it easier for teams to scale securely, integrate new business needs quickly, operate cloud services consistently, and reduce risk through strong architecture, automation, governance, and operational discipline.

You will work closely with Cybersecurity, Network, Platform Engineering, Support Services, business leaders, and key vendors to ensure cloud and systems platforms support how the company operates today and how it needs to grow. Travel to offices or project locations will be required depending on business needs.

Position Details

Cloud Architecture & Platform Strategy

Lead the development and governance of enterprise cloud architecture with primary focus on Microsoft Azure, M365 foundational services, and cloud-first infrastructure capabilities.
Define and enforce standards for cloud compute, storage, platform services, tenant configuration, cloud-side networking dependencies, and core enterprise systems.
Establish repeatable architecture patterns, landing zones, naming standards, tagging standards, service models, and reference architectures that support growth and consistency.
Drive modernization through infrastructure-as-code, automation, standardized service deployment, and simplification of legacy or inconsistent system practices.
Ensure cloud architecture balances scalability, security, cost efficiency, resilience, and operational supportability.
Provide technical direction for cloud platform decisions, ensuring designs align with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity standards, and business priorities.
Translate business growth plans into practical cloud and systems roadmap decisions that can scale across divisions, offices, and project environments.

Identity & Access Management

Own the enterprise identity strategy as a core control plane for access, security, and platform integration.
Lead governance of Entra ID, authentication methods, role-based access control, conditional access, identity lifecycle management, and enterprise access patterns.
Partner with Cybersecurity to align privileged access, zero trust enforcement, identity protection, and access monitoring with enterprise security requirements.
Ensure identity services are designed to scale with organizational growth, acquisitions, new offices, new applications, and changing compliance requirements.
Establish standards for administrative access, service accounts, groups, application integrations, and identity-related operational processes.
Drive consistent identity practices across M365, Azure, SaaS integrations, infrastructure platforms, and business-facing services.

Cloud Operations & Reliability

Own the operational performance, reliability, and availability of cloud and systems platforms under the Cloud/Systems function.
Establish monitoring, alerting, logging, and observability practices that allow teams to detect issues early and reduce business impact.
Lead operational maturity efforts including incident response coordination, problem management, root cause analysis, change management, and continuous improvement.
Define and enforce configuration management, lifecycle management, backup, recovery, patching, and service health practices for cloud and systems platforms.
Ensure operational practices are scalable and repeatable rather than dependent on tribal knowledge or one-off manual processes.
Partner with Support and Platform Engineering to ensure clean handoffs, escalation paths, and visibility into platform issues that impact users.

Automation & Infrastructure Engineering

Drive automation of infrastructure provisioning, platform configuration, reporting, and recurring operational tasks.
Establish infrastructure-as-code standards using appropriate tools such as Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or similar automation frameworks.
Promote reusable templates, modules, scripts, and deployment patterns that improve consistency and reduce manual effort.
Align infrastructure automation with change management, auditability, access control, and operational governance requirements.
Support the development of automated workflows for provisioning, deprovisioning, system configuration, and compliance reporting.
Create an engineering culture that favors repeatable, documented, and measurable solutions over ad hoc administration.

M365 Platform Governance & Administration

Own administration and platform governance of M365 foundational services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Exchange Online, OneDrive, and related tenant-level capabilities.
Ensure M365 services are configured consistently with enterprise standards for security, retention, provisioning, lifecycle management, and service integration.
Partner with Technology Delivery to support collaboration capabilities while maintaining Cloud/Systems ownership of tenant configuration, platform controls, and technical governance.
Define guardrails for site provisioning, storage, sharing, lifecycle, service settings, and administrative ownership across M365 services.
Support data governance requirements by implementing platform-level controls for retention, classification dependencies, auditability, and access management.
Ensure M365 configuration decisions are documented, supportable, and aligned with Cybersecurity, Legal, Compliance, and business needs.

Security & Compliance Integration

Partner with Cybersecurity to ensure cloud and systems platforms meet enterprise security, data protection, and compliance expectations.
Support implementation of controls for logging, monitoring, audit readiness, vulnerability management, secure configuration, and incident response.
Ensure cloud and systems platforms align with zero trust principles and applicable frameworks such as NIST, CMMC, or other regulatory requirements.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries between Cloud/Systems platform controls, Cybersecurity policy and monitoring, and Technology Delivery business enablement. Drive remediation of platform risks related to identity, configuration drift, excessive permissions, unsupported services, and inconsistent administration practices.

Vendor, Licensing & Cloud Financial Management

Manage relationships with cloud providers, Microsoft, service partners, and key enterprise platform vendors.
Oversee cloud consumption, licensing, cost visibility, and cost optimization practices in partnership with Finance, Procurement, and technology leadership.
Establish FinOps-aligned practices for cost accountability, forecasting, service usage review, and optimization of cloud and M365 investments.
Evaluate vendor capabilities, platform roadmaps, and service changes to determine practical value and risk for Southland.
Ensure contracts, licensing models, and platform decisions support scalability, reliability, compliance, and responsible cost management.

Leadership, Team Development & Governance

Build and lead a high-performing Cloud/Systems organization, including cloud engineering, systems engineering, identity, and M365 platform administration capabilities.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, service ownership, performance expectations, and development paths for team members.
Set priorities, manage staffing and budget needs, and align team capacity with enterprise initiatives and operational commitments.
Promote a culture of accountability, standardization, automation, documentation, and continuous improvement.
Serve as a strategic advisor to Infrastructure leadership by clearly communicating risks, tradeoffs, roadmap needs, resource constraints, and business impacts.
Develop governance practices that allow the organization to move quickly while maintaining secure, reliable, and supportable platforms.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, enterprise infrastructure, or related technology leadership roles.
5+ years of experience leading technical teams, including responsibility for planning, staffing, performance management, budgeting, and prioritization of work.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure, M365, Entra ID, and cloud-first enterprise platform operations.
Deep understanding of identity and access management, including authentication, RBAC, conditional access, privileged access, group strategy, and identity lifecycle processes.
Experience designing and operating scalable cloud environments that support distributed companies, rapid growth, multiple offices, and diverse business needs.
Strong understanding of cloud operations, monitoring, incident response, change management, lifecycle management, backup/recovery, and service reliability practices.
Experience with infrastructure automation and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or similar platforms.

Description

The Senior Director of Enterprise Data Partners (EDP) – Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for the development, governance, and delivery of enterprise data and analytics products supporting revenue cycle, finance strategy, and accounting across the Mount Sinai Health System.

Operating within a center-led, data product model, this role oversees multidisciplinary teams of data product managers, data analysts, and developers/data science analysts for delivering trusted data products including dashboards, reporting, predictive analytics, and self-service capabilities that improve financial performance and operational decision-making for the enterprise.

The Senior Director serves as the primary data and analytics partner to executive finance leadership, working collaboratively with business owners, data engineering, epic teams, digital and AI, and other DTP teams to ensure seamless product delivery and implementation. They are responsible for development of the data strategy, establishing product roadmaps, and ensuring the delivery of scalable data products in partnership with finance teams while promoting standardization, governance, Agile delivery, and measurable business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Define and execute the enterprise data product strategy for finance (revenue cycle, finance strategy, accounting), aligning initiatives to health system priorities and measurable business outcomes.
Own and scale a portfolio of enterprise data products and sources of truth, including datasets, semantic layers, dashboards, and benchmarking-integrated assets, with accountability for product vision, adoption, standardization, governance, and measurable impact on financial and operational outcomes and business value.
Partner with Finance executives to translate strategic priorities into data product roadmaps and clear delivery timelines.
Lead the transition to a product-based, agile operating model, embedding cross-functional teamwork, lifecycle accountability, and iterative delivery to drive value.
Oversee integration and optimization of internal and external data assets, including EMR, claims, and benchmarking data, enabling longitudinal and cross-continuum analytics.
Drive adoption of advanced analytics and AI-enabled capabilities that support proactive operational decision-making.
Standardize and govern enterprise metric definitions, data models, and analytics assets, reducing fragmentation, eliminating duplication, and strengthening data quality and trust in partnership with the Director of Data Governance.
Collaborate across Enterprise Data Partner leadership to enhance data architecture, optimize pipelines, and support enterprise analytics infrastructure.
Serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership, guiding enterprise analytics investments, benchmarking strategy, and opportunities to improve quality and outcomes.
Drive enterprise adoption, enablement, and value realization of data products, ensuring alignment to measurable performance improvement and system-wide priorities.
Recruit, mentor, and lead a high-performing, multidisciplinary team, fostering a product-oriented culture of innovation, accountability, agility, and continuous improvement.
Ensure compliance with all applicable regulatory, privacy, security, and governance requirements, including HIPAA and clinical data standards.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Biostatistics, Health Informatics, Computer/Data Science, or a related field required.
Master’s or Doctoral degree preferred (e.g., MBA, MHA, MS in Data Science, PhD, MD with finance/analytics experience).
Background or certification in healthcare quality, informatics, or data science is highly desirable.

Experience Requirements

15 years of progressive information systems management experience preferably in a health care field.

Other Experience Specific To Position

10–15 years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare quality reporting and data science, with at least 5 years in finance or revenue cycle analytics for an academic health system or teaching hospital.
Demonstrated success managing teams in a multi-mission environment (clinical, operational, finance, academic).
Demonstrated success leading enterprise-scale analytics or data product organizations with accountability for domain strategy, adoption, and business outcomes.
Familiarity with AI/ML applications in healthcare analytics and decision support.
Expertise in healthcare finance and related software, data, and tools.
